_about: EN-only golden set for the work-history extraction eval. Each case mirrors the real extraction schema (services/nlp_service.py SYSTEM_PROMPT) in `expected`. Scoring contract used by scripts/eval_models.py: work_experience entries are greedy-matched to expected by `category`, then `duration`/`duration_unit` are exact-matched ONLY when present in expected (so omission cases test presence of the entry, not a duration). availability.schedule days are set-F1'd; per matched day, start/end are exact-matched. `shift_preference` is exact-matched when present. `notes_contains` is a list of substrings that must appear in availability.notes (the day-less-hours fallback). Free-text fields (work_type, employer, context, summary) are reported by the scorer but NOT gated.

_normalization_notes.year_and_half: 'a year and a half' normalizes to 18 months (integer, smallest whole unit). This is NOT arbitrary: the review step persists duration via parseInt (blueprints/onboarding/static/onboarding/js/review.js), which truncates any fraction — so '1.5 years' is silently corrupted to '1 year' on save, while '18 months' round-trips losslessly. 18 months is therefore the only representation the pipeline can actually store, making it the correct target. SYSTEM_PROMPT now instructs models to convert fractional lengths to the smaller whole unit. A model emitting 1.5 years is genuinely wrong (lossy), not just stylistically different.
_normalization_notes.omitted_duration: Cases with no stated length omit `duration`/`duration_unit` in expected; the scorer does not score those fields, so the case tests whether the work entry is produced at all.
